messages:
maya: quick sync — following up on the org-bound API key handshake we discussed in the RFC. want to nail down compatibility + migration approach.
jon: tl;dr: we need deterministic derivation for operator keys + a runtime binding check for pinned orgs.
rashid: can you sketch the handshake? was thinking: client sends key_id + X-Org header + signature over (key_id||org||nonce). server verifies signature using public key for key_id then asserts org in allowed_orgs[key_id].
lina: that feels right. i worry about legacy keys that are not org-anchored — we have many integrations. fallback path?
maya: plan A: new header X-Org and signature required for new keys. Plan B (migration): allow legacy keys but emit metric and 401 after N days if request includes org header but key not bound.
jon: +1. also recommend a soft-fail mode where we log and tag requests as "unbound" for 14 days, then block. we should surface via console.
rashid: implementation note: token table add column org_allowlist (json array) and derived_pub_key (hex) for deterministic derived keys. that lets runtime avoid extra lookups for common cases.
lina: DB change ok but add backfill job. backfill approach: for keys issued before YYYY-MM-DD set org_allowlist=null and migration_tag=legacy.
maya: rollout plan: deploy server checks (soft-log) -> enable canary 5% -> increase to 50% with migration UI -> block for 100% after 30 days. docs + SDKs published before 50%.
jon: auth-bot: please run simulated load against canary config and post latency/failure delta.
auth-bot: sim run queued. expected additions: 0.6ms p95 per auth check, 0.8% increase in 429s under peak due to extra DB reads.
rashid: optimize: cache derived_pub_key in redis for 1m, and prefetch org_allowlist for active key_ids. should kill that p95 delta.
lina: question: should we require org header for internal traffic? some internal services call multiple orgs in one request path.
maya: internal services can still call with project-scoped tickets; we won't break internal until next quarter. this handshake targets customer-facing API keys first.
jon: security tradeoff: derived keys reduce blast radius if operator leaks base private key? if derivation is per-org then yes — but we must use HKDF with domain separation. pseudo: `derived_key = HKDF(base_key, info="redwood.org."||org_id)`
rashid: agree. also rotation: rotate base_key will rotate derived keys — need to version derivation (kdf_v). add kdf_version to token metadata.
lina: UX: in console, add a "Bind to orgs" checkbox with autocomplete. default: unbound (legacy), new keys default to bound to the creator org.
maya: follow-up tasks: 1) draft migration playbook (owner: lina) 2) db migration PR (owner: rashid) 3) SDK header helpers + example (owner: jon) 4) telemetry dashboard (owner: maya)
jon: i'll open PRs for SDKs, include snippet: ```js
// client helper
const sig = sign(key, `${keyId}|${orgId}|${nonce}`)
fetch('/v1/finish', { headers: { 'Authorization': `ApiKey ${keyId}`, 'X-Org': orgId, 'X-Sig': sig } })
```
lina: any objections to the 30-day hard block timeline?
rashid: suggest make it 45 days to give enterprise customers time.
maya: ok 45 days. capture in playbook.
jon: noted. i'll sync with sales for enterprise exceptions.
auth-bot: sim complete: canary config steady at 5% no regressions after caching tweaks. posting metrics to #canary-metrics. :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks all. next check-in on migration playbook Friday. :thumbsup:
